summary: The 'modex' project aims to create an MCP server for Go, similar to Rust's 'cratedex', to enhance LLM capabilities in writing modern, idiomatic Go code. It will address current gaps in existing Go MCP solutions by offering indexed documentation search with FTS5, comprehensive diagnostics (build, lint, security, outdated, modernization), and version-aware modernization guidance via `go fix` integration. The project will specifically tackle common LLM Go failure modes like compilation issues, concurrency bugs, version skew, dependency hallucination, and stale idioms. The technical stack will leverage Go 1.25+, the official Go MCP SDK, SQLite with FTS5, and deep integration with standard Go tooling. Key outputs include a suite of MCP tools for project registration, documentation search, various diagnostics, and modernization application, alongside a 'coding_modern_go' prompt.

bugs: LLMs generate Go code with compilation blockers (missing imports, incorrect assignments, test package misuse).
LLMs often introduce concurrency bugs (WaitGroup misuse, deadlocks, goroutine leaks).
LLMs exhibit version skew, denying the existence of newer Go APIs.
LLMs hallucinate non-existent Go packages (dependency hallucination).
LLMs produce Go code with stale idioms, resisting modern patterns even when directed.
ideas: Develop 'modex' as an MCP server for LLM-assisted Go development.
Implement a full-text search (FTS5) index for Go documentation (stdlib + dependencies).
Provide comprehensive diagnostics, including build errors, vet warnings, lint issues, outdated dependencies, security vulnerabilities, and modernization opportunities.
Integrate with `go fix` to analyze and apply code modernization transformations.
Create a 'coding_modern_go' prompt to guide LLMs on modern Go idioms, features, and best practices.
Ensure all recommendations and analyses are version-aware, respecting the project's `go.mod` file.
Design the system to be lightweight, with fast startup and background indexing.
Defensively address known LLM failure modes in Go code generation.
constraints: Utilize the `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` for MCP server implementation.
Support stdio and HTTP/SSE for communication transport.
Employ SQLite with FTS5 for documentation storage and search.
Integrate with existing Go tooling: `go doc`, `go vet`, `go fix`, `go list`, `gopls`, `govulncheck`.
Adopt a Go-native architecture, potentially inspired by 'cratedex' but adapted for Go.
domains: Large Language Model (LLM) assistance in software development

actionable_pointers: Define and implement the proposed MCP tools: `register_project`, `search_docs`, `get_diagnostics`, `get_build_diagnostics`, `get_outdated_diagnostics`, `get_security_diagnostics`, `get_modernize_diagnostics`, `apply_modernize`, `get_go_version_info`, and `list_modules`.
Develop the `coding_modern_go` prompt content, covering Go 1.25/1.26 features, modern idioms, blessed packages, and common mistakes.
Set up the core technical stack: Go 1.25+ project, integrate the `go-sdk`, and establish SQLite with FTS5 for documentation indexing.
Design and implement the integration points for `go fix` analysis and application, either programmatically via `go/analysis` or by shelling out.
Analyze existing Go MCP servers (godoc-mcp, gopls MCP, mcp-gopls, go-dev-mcp, mcp-language-server) to identify specific features to replicate or improve upon in 'modex'.
